description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to Use Class C4 (HMO-house in multiple occupation), with single storey rear extension, rear dormer to outrigger, front roof lights, with associated amenity, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:PlansE00P00P01P02P03P04P05P06P07Flood Risk AssessmentReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to first occupation of the HMO, Cycle parking, shall be provided as indicated on drawing P06, in accordance with the following requirements:- Provision of a minimum of SIX long stay cycle parking spaces;- in an accessible location; the store door must have a minimum opening width of 1.2m- long stay cycle parking spaces secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob;- fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof.Reason: To ensure the provision of accessible, secure, and adequate cycle parking facilities and to safeguard the character and appearance of the area.

Prior to occupation of the development, the refuse storage facilities shown on drawing number P07 shall be provided in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.Reason: In the interests of amenity and the recycling of waste materials in support of the Boroughs waste reduction targets.

The use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation hereby approved shall be occupied by a maximum of 6 people at any one time and shall not be subdivided or occupied as self-contained units. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

No cooking facilities, including hot plates, shall be installed in the bedrooms of the development hereby permitted unless details have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Any cooking facilities shall thereafter only be implemented in accordance with the details that have been approved pursuant to this condition.Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans, prior to commencement of the development, a revised ground floor plan showing the communal kitchen/dining/living room laid out with the dining and living areas positioned nearer to the internal exit from the room than the kitchen and cooking facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved layout shall be implemented prior to first occupation of the HMO and retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory means of escape and a good quality communal kitchen/dining/living area for future occupiers, in accordance with Policies DMD5 and DMD8 and the Council's HMO Standards.

The development shall not be occupied until details of source control SuDS have been submitted and approved by the Local Authority. Source control SuDS measures include green roofs, rain gardens and permeable paving. The details must include plans, specifications and maintenance information. The developer should use the SuDS Proforma for minor developers found on our webpage https://www.enfield.gov.uk/services/planning/sustainable-drainage-systems to assistthem through our requirements.REASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value
